skill.name: cursor
skill.description: Use Cursor from the command line to open projects, files, diffs, workspaces, settings, and extension tools.
skill.summary: Command-line reference for opening and managing Cursor editor workflows.
skill.author: Dicklesworthstone

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, inline command names, and a documented SSH config path. No executable code, prompt injection, credential access, or data exfiltration intent was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Command examples may be mistaken for executable automation by scanners.
remediation.suggestion: Keep commands clearly inside documentation examples and avoid wording that directs agents to run them without user confirmation.

remediation.issue: The SSH configuration path references a sensitive user directory.
remediation.suggestion: Clarify that the path is informational and should not be read or modified unless the user explicitly asks.

content.value_statement: Developers often need quick Cursor commands without searching external documentation. This skill provides concise CLI guidance for files, folders, diffs, windows, extensions, and remote setup.
actual_capabilities: Shows how to open files, folders, and projects in Cursor from the command line.
Documents line and column targeting for direct navigation to source locations.
Explains new window, reuse window, wait mode, and diff mode options.
Lists extension management commands for installing, removing, disabling, and listing extensions.
Identifies settings, keybindings, user data, extensions directory, and SSH remote configuration locations.
limitations: It documents Cursor CLI usage but does not install Cursor or verify the local binary path.
It does not automate GUI actions inside Cursor after the editor opens.
Remote development guidance is limited to the configuration location and GUI entry points.
Some paths are platform-specific and may need adjustment on non-macOS systems.

use_cases.title: Open a project quickly
use_cases.description: Launch a repository, folder, or specific source file in Cursor directly from a terminal workflow.

use_cases.title: Review file differences
use_cases.description: Use Cursor diff mode to compare two files while staying in an editor-centered review flow.

use_cases.title: Manage editor extensions
use_cases.description: Find commands for listing, installing, uninstalling, or disabling Cursor extensions during environment setup.

prompt_templates.title: Open the current project
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me the Cursor CLI command to open the current directory.

prompt_templates.title: Open a file at a line
prompt_templates.prompt: How do I open a specific file in Cursor at line 42 from the terminal?

prompt_templates.title: Compare two files
prompt_templates.prompt: Give me the Cursor CLI command to compare two files in diff mode.

prompt_templates.title: Configure advanced launch options
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain Cursor CLI options for a new window, reuse window, wait mode, user data directory, and extensions directory.

output_examples.input: I need to open a project in a new Cursor window.
output_examples.output: Use the new-window option with the project path. This opens the folder separately instead of reusing the active window.

output_examples.input: I want Cursor to wait while I edit a git message.
output_examples.output: Use wait mode as the editor command. Cursor stays attached until the file is closed, which works for commit messages.

output_examples.input: I need to compare two local files.
output_examples.output: Use Cursor diff mode with the two file paths. Cursor opens a visual comparison for review.

best_practices: Confirm paths before opening files or folders from automation.
Use wait mode when Cursor is acting as an editor for another command.
Review extension identifiers before installing or uninstalling extensions.
anti_patterns: Do not run Cursor commands that modify global settings without user confirmation.
Do not read or edit SSH configuration unless the user explicitly requests it.
Do not assume macOS settings paths apply to every operating system.

faq.question: What does this skill help me do?
faq.answer: It helps you use the Cursor command-line interface to open files, projects, diffs, workspaces, and extension tools.

faq.question: Does it install Cursor?
faq.answer: No. It assumes Cursor is already installed and available through the cursor command.

faq.question: Can it open a file at a specific line?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill documents file path formats that include line and column positions.

faq.question: Can it manage extensions?
faq.answer: Yes. It lists commands for viewing, installing, uninstalling, and disabling Cursor extensions.

faq.question: Does it support remote development?
faq.answer: It notes that Cursor supports remote development similar to VS Code and points to the SSH configuration location.

faq.question: Is this skill safe to use?
faq.answer: The reviewed file is documentation only. Users should still confirm commands before changing settings, extensions, or sensitive configuration files.
